label: anch-costslide-century
_why: THE COST SLIDE (user-ruled 2026-09-20, 'go with C^era', after the eight-industry anchor slide at in0 1.2 was BROKEN BY STALL in 3 of 3 century runs at world GDP 0.55 / 0.65 / 0.64x). The slide alone halves what a rung produces and leaves its price alone, so capital per unit of output DOUBLES for the slid set - measured at 1935, slid e3 ran 0.42 construction points per pound of realised value added against the unslid 0.21 and the canon's own 0.21. Each building makes half the value, so GDP per building halves, so construction, tax and the investment pool are all proportionally smaller (pool 331M against the canon's 2,365M at the SAME 0.61 construction levels per million of GDP), so fewer buildings are built - and JOBS SCALE WITH BUILDINGS, because employment per level is vanilla's and untouched. The measured result was productivity 1.28x vanilla and productive workers per capita 0.53x. This arm makes building_cost follow the anchor, using the same exponent output and input already use.
_arm: probe-anch-costslide: identical to probe-anch-in12 except building_cost on the eight slid industries, which now pays anchor x C^(era-1). FIELD DIFF: building_cost on 21 rungs, nothing else. textile/tooling/glass/furniture e0 316, e1 600, e2 1140, e3 2166; automotive e2 1520, e3 2888; electrics e2 1520; munition e1 800, e2 1520. ai_value deliberately does NOT slide, so this stays one lever - a slid e3 keeping ai_value 27,000 while costing 2,166 is unusually attractive and is a thing to watch in the result, not to pre-empt.
_e0_is_intended: The clean exponent also takes the slid e0 rungs from 600 to 316 (k = -1). RAISED WITH THE USER AND CONFIRMED INTENDED ('600 to 316 is intended'). Those rungs produce anchor / A too, so it is consistent; the risk is that cheaper buildings are easier to build and e0 is the rung the design wants dead. It cannot rescue the 17% of e0 levels already loss-making (payback on a negative profit stays infinite) and it moves e0 payback only 69.7 -> 36.7 years.
_n: 2+1: two runs, then alignment_check.mjs, a third ONLY on divergence (the standard). The register HARD lines apply per run through stop_watch.

_predictions._basis: The stalled arm at n=3, the canon at n=3, and the STATIC payback table (profit per level held at what the run recorded - an UPPER BOUND, since a cheaper building gets built more and that shrinks the profit in the denominator). Stated before the runs.
_predictions.the_user_expectation: THE USER EXPECTS THIS TO BE INSUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN, and said so before the launch: the change is not expected to be enough without an A and B change. Recorded so the result reads against it either way.
_predictions.world_gdp: The stalled arm read 0.55 / 0.65 / 0.64x. Restoring capital efficiency to the canon's parity should move it up; the canon sits at 1.09-1.10x with that efficiency. PREDICT 0.75-1.15x - most likely still short of the 1.0 aim but out of the hard stall band (floor 0.66x). A reading ABOVE 1.38x is the runaway ceiling and would say the cost cut overshot.
_predictions.workers: THE KEY ONE, because labour was the whole of the shortfall (0.53x at 1935 against productivity 1.28x). Jobs scale with buildings and the slid rungs are 1.9x cheaper, so PREDICT productive workers per capita 0.60-0.75x - up from 0.53 but probably still under the register's 0.6-0.95 aim at the world level.
_predictions.the_gains_must_survive: Cost enters neither output nor inputs, so PREDICT the 1836 anchor error, the base-price margin ladder and F97's death test are UNCHANGED by construction, and the measured gains hold: steel at 69% of base and engines at 96% at 1935 (vanilla 106 and 128), T0 falling every decade to about 2% of tiered employment, productivity above vanilla. If the PRICE DECLINE WEAKENS, the extra supply is being absorbed by extra demand and the mechanism is not what this arm assumes.
_predictions.payback: STATIC and an upper bound: the slid frontier goes 9.5 -> 5.0 years at 1935, automotive and electrics to 2.9-3.4. Faster than anything in the book bar the art academy. PREDICT the realised figures land LONGER than that, because more building means more supply and less profit - and if they do not, the arm is heading for the runaway ceiling.

_comparison: probe-anch-in12 at n=3 (20260919_224153) is the paired arm and differs in building_cost ALONE; the canon at n=3 (20260917_132449 + 20260917_161410) and vanilla n=16 (20260821_131149) are the references. WARNING: the canon lacks the urban-centre electricity override that both anchor arms carry, so an arm-vs-canon reading holds two differences; arm-vs-arm holds one and arm-vs-vanilla holds none.
_watch: run 1 at ~5 min: PM_TECH_REHAUL marker, game version, this run's error window BY POSITION (parsed stamps, wrap-safe), clock advancing
run 1 at ~10 min: queue_mix.mjs on the first summary - and here especially, because cheaper slid buildings could crowd a major's queue
first_run_decomp.mjs after run 1, before the batch completes (the standing ruling)
post-batch: preflight -Session, criteria.mjs, alignment_check.mjs for the third run, VERDICT.md, SESSION_VERDICTS, FINDINGS
_cost: 2 runs x 1836->1936 at roughly 2.5 h each, plus a third only on divergence: 5-8 hours.
_caveats: TWO RUNS is the 2+1 standard, not a description of a book: world GDP at the end state has a wide seed spread (F114).
The anchor slide itself still needs a BALANCE_FRAMEWORK ruling before a book of this shape could go canon.
ROADMAP step 8 P2's electricity override rides along, as in the paired arm.
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent.

defaults._dump_dates_note: Identical to canon-n7, the solver2 family, the F79 vanilla baseline and every four-rung arm - what keeps the sessions comparable.
defaults._tags_note: ⭐ GER, BEL and NGF ADDED 2026-09-20 (user-ruled). The old list GBR/FRA/USA/PRU/RUS/JAP/NET could not answer a per-MARKET question about Germany or Belgium: the Prussian market drops out of the telemetry after 1870 when PRU becomes NGF then GER, and Belgium was never instrumented at all - so markets.tsv carries no German prices after 1870 and no Belgian prices ever, and the true-margin table of 2026-09-20 could only be produced for GBR, USA and NET. PRU/NGF/GER are the SAME state in its three forms and all three are needed to follow one market across the century. Cost: about 1,800 extra log lines a run (3 markets x 12 dump dates x ~50 goods), which is nothing against the ring. ⚠ This changes the telemetry the mod is built with, so a run under this list is NOT byte-identically instrumented to runs 1 and 2 of 20260920_114003 - see anch_costslide_tb.json, which deliberately keeps the old list for that pair tie-breaker.
